verdicts.note: Sitting appointed sheriff [S5], seven years as undersheriff [S6], nearly 20 years in the office and running on continuity [S1]; maximal proven-record profile, documented in official and statement sources.

S3 pairs drug and gang enforcement and visible presence with prevention, crisis and behavioral-health partnerships and advocacy for community behavioral-health access; enforcement-leaning but not fully pole_a, so -1 medium holds.
First run for office from outside the Douglas office, explicitly against 'the status quo' [S1][S5]; 20 years of law enforcement and a former patrol-chief post keep it at +1 rather than +2.

S2 is squarely pole_a: 'Broken Windows' policing, 'zero-tolerance' for gang-type crime handled 'to the fullest extent of the law', and fighting 'the war on drugs'. His mental-health line ('we cannot just pass the issue onto the hospital or the jail') and plan to expand collaborative outreach [S3] do not describe diversion, voluntary treatment or non-police responders, so they do not pull him off the pole. The scoring basis also paraphrases S2 as a response that 'keeps people out of jail', which the dossier does not say. Scoring him the same -1 as Caille hides the difference the _contest.md itself identifies (Musgrove 'more explicitly zero-tolerance'). Medium, not high: the evidence is campaign-site statements, not a record.
